mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% over the next month, investors anticipate higher future inflation, which lowers real equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified FEDFUNDS increase period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs over two consecutive months predicts stronger consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns in the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month's value and PAYEMS current > previous month's value + 50000
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite meeting the PAYEMS threshold for two months.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 450K units for two consecutive months, it indicates resilient consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the two-month HOUST surge.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 96.0 for three consecutive months suggests supply-side weakness, which tends to precede negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or equal to mean during the INDPRO contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (labor market tightness) of at least 0.2% each are interpreted as dual signals of disinflation, which can drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days when the interaction is present.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < previous month's value by >=0.2% AND UNRATE < previous month's value by >=0.2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) despite the dual rate decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 8.0% triggers expectations of weaker wage growth, which can produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days in a non-recessionary economy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the UNRATE decline.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.5% in a single month, it suggests accelerating inflation, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or flat despite CPIAUCSL exceeding the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly decline in GDPC1 (real GDP) of at least 2% over three months indicates economic softening, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days in non-recessionary regimes.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous month's value by >=2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the identified GDP contraction period.
